title: The star cluster Messier 47
caption: The open star cluster Messier 47, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope at La Silla

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: A sprinkling of brilliant blue stars dominates this image of the star cluster Messier 47, with a few contrasting red giant stars among them. The picture was taken with the Wide Field Imager camera at ESO's La Silla Observatory in Chile.

Messier 47 is a young open cluster, a loose group of stars that formed together from the same cloud of gas and dust. A star's colour reveals its surface temperature. The blue stars here are hot, while red giants are cooler stars that have swollen in size late in their lives.

Because all the stars in a cluster share roughly the same age, the mix of colours carries information. The most massive stars evolve fastest, so they are the first to become red giants, while less massive stars stay in their longer, steadier phase for much longer.

understand.summary: This visible-light image from the Wide Field Imager combines B, V and R filters. The colour assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: The blue and red star colours reflect real temperature differences, but long exposures reveal far more stars than the eye could see.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.

explore: The Wide Field Imager is mounted on the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope. The colour picture was built from exposures through B, V and R filters, all in visible light. Messier 47 lies in the direction of the constellation Puppis.
alt: A sprinkling of brilliant blue stars with a few red giant stars among them.
